label: Measure the acts of a comprehending source and a reflective recipient
summary: Comprehension orders whole acts under the existing act-to-knowability and knowing-within-act laws. Applying the comparison at the sole giver gives a new direct support option for the weak represented-esse bound on actual participants, under full measured comprehension of each participant and explicit same-state scale calibration. At a witnessed full self-comprehension the recipient's measured act, knowability and knowing all agree up to preorder equivalence. A higher actual knowing by the source then yields a strict represented-esse inequality on this pair. Positive content-indexed uptake by the source admits a lower source act, ordinary self-knowing with higher source performance admits a tie, and even one-way full comprehension admits a tie. A populated model realizes the positive strict and weak conditions without knowledge above the object's knowability. See docs/notes/modal-spine.md, 'Can measured cognition compare the giver and recipient of esse?'. These formal readings concern actual attainment. No new attribution, general adequacy principle, or universal limited/unlimited calibration follows.
blocker: Weak application needs affirmative warrant that the source comprehends the actual individual to its knowability, beyond one true effect-directed content, and calibration of the same state's whole-act measure at represented esse. Strict application needs a supported ceiling on the recipient's knowability or full self-comprehension at a measured grade, together with a higher source knowing. Explanatory correctness about one's own constitution can tie. Seek an independently warranted degree difference on the selected bearers; reversing the noninfinite-intellect theorem presupposes a nonmaximal act premise.
